concept.name: Momentum indicator
concept.definition: The simplest momentum measure: the absolute point difference between the current close and the close n periods ago, plotted as an unbounded oscillator around zero; the unscaled sibling of the rate-of-change, which expresses the same comparison as a percentage.
concept.intuition: It tracks how many points price gained or lost over the window, ignoring the price level, so its slope shows acceleration or deceleration of the move.
concept.mechanics: Compute Close - Close(n periods ago), conventionally with n around 10-14. Positive values show net gains over the window, negative values net losses; zero-line crosses define the momentum bias.
concept.formula: Momentum(n) = C_t - C_{t-n}; the percentage variant is ROC(n) = ((C_t - C_{t-n}) / C_{t-n}) x 100.
concept.failure_modes: Being unscaled in points, readings are not comparable across securities or across large price changes in one security; like ROC it whipsaws around zero in sideways markets.
concept.misconceptions: Momentum indicators describe past speed; a high positive reading can persist or reverse without warning and is not a prediction of continued gains.
concept.example: Close today 55, close 12 days ago 50: momentum = +5 points, whereas the rate of change is +10%.
